content.title: About
content.content: French toast is a dish made from slices of bread soaked in a mixture of eggs, milk, sugar and spices, then fried on a pan until golden brown. It is traditionally served with syrup, berries, fruit or a dusting of powdered sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in Europe during the Middle Ages and was originally called “fried bread”.
In the United States French toast gained popularity in the early 20th century thanks to mass‑produced ready mixes.
There are many variations, including additions of cinnamon, vanilla, rum or even cheese.
In some countries, such as Japan, it is served with soy sauce and seaweed.
The classic French recipe uses a baguette, which makes the toast extra crisp.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Eggs in the batter provide complete protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Milk adds calcium, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Thanks to eggs and milk, French toast is rich in vitamins B2, B6 and B12, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from bread and fats from butter quickly replenishes energy stores.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Adding cinnamon or berries supplies additional antioxidants.

items.title: Egg or milk allergy
items.content: People with food allergies may react to these ingredients.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Traditional recipes often contain sugar; individuals with diabetes should reduce it.

items.title: Calorie rich
items.content: Frying in butter adds calories, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Bread contains gluten, making the dish unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve French toast hot, drizzled with maple syrup, honey, berry sauce, or dusted with powdered sugar. It pairs well with fresh fruit, yogurt or nuts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed immediately. Leftovers can be cooled, placed in an airtight container, and stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat by briefly toasting in a pan.
